subject: Propagating site specific uncertainty from inla outputs into an occupancy model

messages.author: 11f741253673c9e0
messages.subject: Propagating site specific uncertainty from inla outputs into an occupancy model
parts:
Hi,

 

I am working in a framework where i am using the outputs (hunting intensity-"mean") from my inla model as a site covariate in an occupancy model. I would however like to propagate the uncertainty associated with the site specific inla outputs into my occupancy model. 

 

1. INLA summary.fitted.values returns the 'mean' and 'sd' - can i use these values to parameterise a normal distribution for hunting intensity at each site in my occupancy model (built in a Bayesian framework – at each iteration it will draw from the site specific distribution) ; and is it correct to assume a normal distribution with the outputted mean and sd? My inla hunting model is built on a negative binomial distribution with one covariate (distance from village) + intercept term.

 

2. The inla.posterior.sample: Is it correct to interpret that this function returns draws from the posterior distribution and the "latent" element is the correct output to extract my intercept and distance.village covariate? 

 

I’m also not clear how the posterior draws correspond to my sites as each draw has only one intercept and covariate term; not the expected X number of sites.

 

Any guidance would be most appreciated.

 

Anand

you can also look at the posterior.marginals for which gives you the
computed posterior marginals,  you may, as an approximation, use a
Gaussian with these mean and stdev. you will not be able get the
dependence between those using this approach

> 2. The inla.posterior.sample: Is it correct to interpret that this
> function returns draws from the posterior distribution and the
> "latent" element is the correct output to extract my intercept and
> distance.village covariate?

this function produce samples from the (approximated) posterior. yes,
you should find what you're looking for in the latent section. if not,
let me know.

> I’m also not clear how the posterior draws correspond to my sites as
> each draw has only one intercept and covariate term; not the expected
> X number of sites.

maybe its the 'Predictor' you need ? 

Best
